code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import sum, avg, max, min, count

trips.groupBy("VendorID").agg(
  count("*").alias("trip_count"),
  sum("fare_amount").alias("total_fare"),
  avg("fare_amount").alias("avg_fare"),
  max("trip_distance").alias("longest_trip"),
).show()
caption: The real payoff over Lesson 53's plain .count() — as many stats as you want.

code:
trips.agg(
  avg("fare_amount").alias("overall_avg_fare"),
  max("trip_distance").alias("overall_max_distance"),
).show()

# treats the whole DataFrame as ONE group -- one row back
caption: The PySpark equivalent of Lesson 23's Pandas df["col"].mean().
count(*) includes nulls; count(col) counts only non-null values.
